summary: Henry Steel Olcott was a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who attended Columbia University from circa 1847 to 1849. He later founded the Theosophical Society in 1875.

Henry Sullivan Jarrett worked in Indology and history and archaeology after studying at Prior Park College. He served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners at Fort William (1870-1894) and Assistant Secretary in the Legislative Department.

Henry Thoby Prinsep worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Tonbridge School and the East India Company College before serving in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1809 to 1843.

Indologist Henry Thomas Colebrooke studied under Citrapati. He served the East India Company (~1782-1814), held judicial and council posts, taught Sanskrit at Fort William College, and served as Director of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823-1837), which he founded.

Henry Thomas Francis worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. After earning his B.A. at the University of Cambridge and studying under Edward Byles Cowell, he became a Fellow at Gonville and Caius College and Under-Librarian at Cambridge University Library.

Henry Thomas Rogers was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary from 1848 to 1849. He later served as Principal of the College of Engineering, Guindy, from circa 1869 to 1880.
Indologist Henry White Wallis studied at the University of Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell in 1882. He later served as a Fellow at Gonville and Caius College from circa 1886 to 1887.

Henry Whitehead studied at Eton College, the University of Oxford, Balliol College, and Princeton University. He worked at Buckmaster & Moore, Balliol College, the UK Government, and served at the University of Oxford from 1945 to 1960.
Indologist Henry Whitelock Torrens studied at Christ Church, Oxford, earning a B.A. between 1823 and 1825. He later served as Secretary of The Asiatic Society from 1840 to 1846.

Henry William Byerley Thomson studied at University College London and Jesus College, Cambridge. He later served as Queen’s Advocate of Ceylon at the University of Ceylon in 1858 and as Puisne Judge at the University of Colombo from 1861 to 1867.

Henry Yule worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at University College London and Addiscombe Military Seminar, he served on the Council of India (1875-1889) and presided over the Hakluyt Society and the Royal Asiatic Society.
Heramba Chandra Chackravarty was an Indology scholar who studied under Manindra Mohan Bose. He held a post as a Lecturer at City College, Kolkata, attested in 1977.

Herbert Arthur Popley worked in Indology and religious studies after earning a B.A. from Hackney College. He served as a London Missionary Society missionary starting in 1901, worked with the YMCA in 1921, and founded the Community Training School, Erode.

Herbert Cushing Tolman worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Yale under William Dwight Whitney, later teaching Sanskrit at Wisconsin and North Carolina before serving as Dean at Vanderbilt University (1894-1923).

Herbert Fletcher De Cou specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Michigan and the American School of Classical Studies at Athens, serving as an Instructor of Greek and Sanskrit at Michigan from 1892 to 1893.

Herbert Franke worked in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Bonn, Berlin under Erich Hauer and Erich Haenisch, and Cologne. He was a professor at the University of Munich and President of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences.

Herbert Frederick Samman was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Emmanuel College from circa 1890 to 1892. He later served as a Lecturer in Bengali at the University of Cambridge from 1922 to 1935.

Herbert Galton, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at the University of Vienna in 1935 under Nikolai Trubetzkoy and Wilhelm Geiger. He later served as Professor of Slavic Linguistics at the University of Kansas from 1962 to 1988.

Herbert Hope Risley worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Winchester College and New College, Oxford, and served as Permanent Secretary of the Judicial Department at the India Office in 1910.

Herbert Härtel specialized in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate at Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He served as Director of the Museum of Asian Art (1963-1986) and Honorary Professor at the Free University of Berlin.
